_comment: Class of Service and capacity policy. This file is the deterministic authorization boundary: the LLM supervisor cannot change it, and anything not granted here is denied. A missing file yields the same posture as an empty one - no external dialing anywhere. Routing DATA (extensions, DIDs, ring groups, symbolic targets) lives in each tenant's routing file, not here - this file only says what is PERMITTED, never what a name means. A leftover "symbolic_targets" key here is a hard startup error.

default._comment: channel_limit caps concurrent supervised calls. It is both cost control and SLA protection: it keeps the first-turn LLM call from queueing past SIP Timer B under load, so calls reject fast (486) rather than dying in a transaction timeout.
default._comment_external: allow_external_dial is default-deny. With it false, every non-'user/' destination is refused no matter what the caller says or the model emits.
default._comment_allowlist: Consulted only when allow_external_dial is true. An EMPTY list with external enabled denies everything - deny by omission, never allow-all. Entries match as prefixes against the normalized digits.
default._comment_spend: Spend circuit breaker: external units permitted per tenant. Zero permits no external spend at all, which is the safe default even if allow_external_dial were turned on by mistake.
default._comment_caller_number: The separate hard-gated tool that dials a raw caller-supplied number, bypassing symbolic narrowing. Leave false unless a tenant genuinely needs callback-to-any-number.
